what_happened: Decision (a) vs (b) for the Goals-block harvest contract resolved quickly and with high confidence by finding that lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's extract_goal_names() already implements the exact leading-identifier-run narrowing plan-format.md documents (commit 8d3ab3283, 2026-11-04), tested against the identical failure shape (R7/R8/R14) one day before the measured defect occurred in the sibling script. No new design was needed -- only porting an already-proven algorithm to the second reader.

Empirically confirmed the already-landed CHALLENGE-STATEMENTS-PREFERRED HARVEST (commit 614922216, 2026-11-09) already masks the measured defect for any well-formed must-exist-polarity lean plan (Challenge Statements section present and populated), so the fallback Goals-prose harvest this record narrows is only reachable today for refutation-polarity plans or malformed/legacy plans missing that section. test-lean-plan-compliance-check.sh has zero test coverage of the Challenge-preferred harvest itself (no C20+ case), so a naively-constructed regression fixture for this record's fix could accidentally route through the already-fixed preferred path and pass without exercising the actual fallback-harvest change.

Planning found a consequence the research report missed: a drop-in port of lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's leading-identifier-run algorithm into lean-plan-compliance-check.sh's Goals-prose fallback changes the harvested name set for FOUR of the suite's 19 existing cases, not zero. Verified empirically by simulating the leading-run algorithm against each case's Goals block: C14 Frame,Short,Tree,hidden -> Frame only; C15 factoring,Frame,Frame.factoring,carrier -> factoring only; C16 drops Mods.Deep; C13 harvests ZERO names (its bullet's first content is prose), flipping its verdict from failed/passed to skipped. The research report's Decisions section asserted this risk 'does not materialize' because the cited fixtures are lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's OWN fixtures and already pass the algorithm -- true, but it did not check lean-plan-compliance-check.sh's own test cases, which deliberately place identifiers in trailing-prose positions. Baseline confirmed green (19/19) before the analysis. The plan now pre-declares the fallout as an atomic-batch phase with three contract-conformance fixture rewrites and one explicit C13 re-baseline, rather than leaving an implementer to discover four red cases mid-phase.

The research report's recommended two-stage bash/grep port of the Python leading-run algorithm was validated empirically during planning before being written into a phase: a single 'grep -oP "^\s*-\s*\K(?:\`IDENT\`|[\s,/]|and\b)+"' stage followed by the script's existing backticked-token re-extraction reproduces the Python's behaviour on the measured-defect shape (yields only foo_bar), on a four-identifier conformant run, and on a prose-leading bullet (yields nothing). This removed the report's top-listed risk (bash/grep drift from the proven Python) from the plan's unknowns at planning time rather than at implementation time.

First verify-touched.sh invocation (Phase 4 scoped Batch Gate Deferral check) reported overall failure via its own verdict line despite the captured run-all.sh tail showing 98 passed/0 failed -- the failing suite/section was above the tail -60 window and the shared working tree was actively being mutated by concurrent sibling tasks (451, 683, etc.) during the multi-minute run, which also auto-backgrounded twice at the harness's ~180s idle/runtime threshold despite an explicit 600000ms Bash-tool timeout and an inner shell timeout below it. A clean full-log re-run (captured to a scratchpad file, no tail truncation) immediately after returned overall_rc 0, 60 suites + 3 owed, 98 passed/0 failed/0 skipped. Treated as sibling-tree-flux noise, not a regression in this task's own lean-plan-compliance-check.sh/test-lean-plan-compliance-check.sh/plan_goals_preamble.md edits, consistent with the dispatch's own concurrency note.
